name: Ecosystem Diversity Management
consequences: Implementing a variety of agricultural practices can enhance food security and resilience against pests. However, this may complicate resource allocation and require more extensive training for personnel managing diverse crops.
options: Adopt permaculture principles to create a self-sustaining agricultural ecosystem that minimizes external inputs and maximizes biodiversity.
Establish monoculture zones for high-efficiency crop production, focusing on staple foods to ensure basic nutritional needs are met.
Integrate aquaponics systems that combine fish farming with plant cultivation, promoting a closed-loop system that conserves water and nutrients.
review: Focusing on monoculture may streamline production but risks food security if a single crop fails, leaving gaps in nutritional diversity.

review: Restricting information may prevent chaos but can also breed suspicion and resentment, leaving gaps in community engagement and trust-building.

review: Centralized management may improve efficiency but risks alienating sectors that feel overlooked, leaving gaps in local adaptability and innovation.
